name: Mythic - Multiplayer C2 Framework
description: Mythic is a modular, Dockerized command-and-control framework with a web UI for multiplayer red-team operations. Its cross-platform agents (Apollo for Windows/.NET, Poseidon for Linux/macOS, etc.) and pluggable C2 profiles (HTTP, SMB, DNS) provide post-exploitation tasking, file transfer, lateral movement, and operator collaboration with full logging.
notes:
=== INSTALL / START ===
  git clone https://github.com/its-a-feature/Mythic ; cd Mythic
  sudo ./mythic-cli start                 # brings up Docker stack; UI on https://<ip>:7443

=== ADD AGENTS + C2 PROFILES ===
  sudo ./mythic-cli install github https://github.com/MythicAgents/Apollo
  sudo ./mythic-cli install github https://github.com/MythicC2Profiles/http

=== OPERATE (web UI) ===
  1. Create a Payload (agent + C2 profile + options) and build it
  2. Host/deliver the payload; agent calls back as a 'callback'
  3. Task callbacks: shell, download/upload, inject, make_token, jump (lateral)
  4. Multiplayer: operators share callbacks; all tasking is logged

=== ADMIN ===
  sudo ./mythic-cli status
  sudo ./mythic-cli config get MYTHIC_ADMIN_PASSWORD

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  Sliver          # single-binary, cross-platform C2
  Havoc           # modern C2 (demon agent)
  Cobalt Strike   # commercial
  dnscat2         # DNS-only tunneling C2

recommended.note: Sliver is a single-binary C2 alternative.
Havoc is a comparable modern C2.
dnscat2 for DNS-only C2 in restrictive egress.

defense.why_it_works: Mythic agents beacon over common protocols (HTTP(S)/DNS/SMB) with configurable jitter and malleable profiles, so C2 traffic blends with normal web/DNS activity and post-exploitation runs as sanctioned-looking process behavior.
defense.prerequisites: Code execution on a target to run the agent, and outbound connectivity to the Mythic server.
defense.impact: Persistent remote control, data theft, credential access, and lateral movement coordinated across an operator team.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1071.001] Beaconing to a consistent external host at regular intervals (even with jitter); JA3/JARM and TLS-cert anomalies; agent-specific artifacts (Apollo .NET loads, named-pipe SMB C2); unusual parent-child process trees and in-memory injection.
defense.artifacts: Proxy/DNS logs with periodic callbacks to a single host, EDR injection/named-pipe events, TLS fingerprint mismatches, new scheduled tasks/services for persistence.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=proxy
| stats count avg(bytes) as avg_bytes by src_ip, dest_host, bin(_time,1h)
| eventstats stdev(count) as beacon_var by src_ip, dest_host
| where count > 20 AND beacon_var < 2
defense.elastic_kql: network.protocol:(http or dns) and destination.domain:* and event.category:network
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| summarize Count=count(), Intervals=make_list(TimeGenerated) by DeviceName, RemoteUrl, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where Count > 20
defense.prevention: Egress filtering and TLS inspection with JA3/JARM blocking; EDR with in-memory and injection detection; DNS monitoring and sinkholing; application allowlisting (WDAC); network segmentation; hunt for periodic beaconing and malleable-profile indicators.

detections.name: Periodic C2 beaconing to a single external host (Mythic)
detections.logic:
index=proxy
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count avg(bytes) as avg_bytes by _time, src_ip, dest_host
| eventstats stdev(count) as beacon_var by src_ip, dest_host
| where count > 20 AND beacon_var < 2
detections.tuning: Allowlist known SaaS/update endpoints; combine with TLS-fingerprint anomalies
